note: Claude Opus 5.5 subagent, effort max, fresh session; kit copy without calibration/ or CHANGELOG

findings.title: A zero or negative interval hangs forever inside .do() instead of raising
Plain interval jobs pause for about an hour when DST ends, because next runs are naive local wall-clock times
until() with a timezone-aware datetime fails with a raw TypeError
DEBUG log lines include the job's arguments, so secrets passed to jobs reach the logs
No security scanning in CI, and the workflow does not limit its token's permissions
A job that raises is never rescheduled and blocks every due job sorted after it
Calling .do() twice on the same Job registers it twice, so it runs twice per due time
No seam for the clock: next-run logic calls datetime.datetime.now() directly, so tests must replace datetime.datetime process-wide
The Scheduler does not own its job list: Job.do() appends itself to scheduler.jobs, and the module exposes that same list as schedule.jobs
Packaging metadata is split across pyproject.toml, setup.py and setup.cfg
The fluent Job API is unannotated, so typed users get Any from every(...).minutes onward despite py.typed
at()'s tz parameter is annotated Optional[str] but documented and implemented to accept pytz timezone objects
Units and weekdays are free-form strings on public, mutable Job attributes, checked only when the next run is computed
docs/conf.py is 373 lines of Sphinx quickstart boilerplate, 231 of them comment lines, mostly commented-out defaults
Slips in user-facing messages and comments
Job.at() is an 89-line method with cyclomatic complexity 25 that re-derives the format from the unit three times
The seven weekday properties are copy-pasted 11-line blocks that differ only in the day name
Failure paths and a few contracts are untested: no raising job, no zero or negative interval, last_run never asserted
Some error messages mislead: to() reports the opposite of the problem and at() prints a literal {}
Using a timezone without pytz fails with a bare ModuleNotFoundError that does not say what to install
An async def job is accepted and then silently never runs
The README quickstart fails as written: its timezone line needs pytz, which pip install schedule does not install
The usage guide states the wrong first run for every(N).hours.at(): it says 06:20:30, the code runs it at 07:20:30
The DST 'clock moves backwards' example describes the change as 02:00 to 03:00
The API reference omits repeat() and the ScheduleError, ScheduleValueError and IntervalError exceptions, and lists CancelJob under Exceptions
Several snippets fail when run as written: missing imports, and an until() example whose deadlines are already past
Small slips: the README's supported-versions line and run_all()'s docstring
The documented dev setup and test command do not work: pytest will not start in the environment requirements-dev.txt builds, and on Python 3.13 the requirements do not install
No contributor or agent guide in the repository: the dev notes in docs/development.rst never mention tox, which CI actually runs, or how to run one test
Releases are a manual procedure that breaks at its build step and publishes only a wheel
CI runs no linter and type-checks only at mypy's default strictness, so the flake8 check the docs describe is never enforced
No caching or pre-commit hooks: every CI job installs tox and all dependencies from scratch
'OS Independent' is claimed, but CI runs only on Linux and the test suite cannot run on Windows
The build uses setuptools metadata that setuptools has deprecated with a 2027-02-18 deadline, and the setuptools requirement is unbounded
Dependency upkeep is manual: no Dependabot or Renovate, and the one pinned dev tool is a 2020 black with five known advisories
The supported and tested Pythons are out of date: 3.7 to 3.9 are end-of-life, 3.13 and later are not declared, and CI uses deprecated action versions
No __all__: the module's imports (datetime, time, random, re, logging, functools and typing names) are part of its public namespace
No deprecation mechanism or backward-compatibility tests
No thread-safety statement and no lock around the job list, although the docs run run_pending() in a background thread while the main thread keeps going
